Update: The Iconic 3DBenchy Enters the Public Domain



Author: CreativeTools

3DBenchy is a 3D model specifically designed for testing and benchmarking 3D printers. It is a small recognizable object that you can download for free, make and share.

http://www.3dbenchy.com/

Print instructions

Maybe you have seen on some prints the infamous Benchy hull line. We eliminated that in our presliced gcode. Check the article, how we did that.
The Benchy hull line

","created":"2019-05-23T11:23:58.120207+00:00","firstPublish":"2019-05-23T11:24:37+00:00","datePublished":"2025-02-14T09:26:10+00:00","modified":"2025-02-14T09:26:45.114781+00:00","likesCount":22082,"downloadCount":549963,"ratingAvg":"4.9393285372","filesCount":5,"price":null,"user":{"publicUsername":"Prusa Research"},"image":{"filePath":"media/prints/3161/images/20206_70fde6a0-6da1-4522-ba46-25f1bece7199/benchy.jpg"},"license":{"name":"Creative Commons — Public Domain"},"category":{"name":"Test Models"},"tags":[{"name":"boat"},{"name":"test"},{"name":"benchy"},{"name":"testmodel"}]},{"id":"1192178","name":"All Terrain Assault Benchy","slug":"all-terrain-assault-benchy","summary":"Blasting into public domain!","description":"

This is what happens when Benchy enters public domain during a mini robots design contest!

In the spirit of Benchy's original purpose as a benchmark test, this variant will also help you test out settings for printing my other jointed models.

 

Print the main body just like a normal Benchy, with whatever material and print settings you want to try out. Your slicer's default 0.2mm profile should be good for a start.

For the rest of the parts, I recommend ABS/ASA or PETG. (Go ahead and try PLA if you want - then wait a week and see how loose the joints get!) Print 6 each of the leg and foot parts, and 2 each of the sockets and cannons.

The sample model was printed using Prusament Galaxy Red PLA and Prusament Galaxy Black ASA.

 

This model is released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license, which allows commercial use with attribution. You can provide proper attribution by including the following statement:

All Terrain Assault Benchy © 2025 by Lucky 13 Toys is licensed under CC BY 4.0

This model is also based on the original 3D Benchy created by Daniel Norée for Creative Tools, in compliance with the CC0 1.0 public domain license.

 

Lastly, if this free model brings you joy (or profit), please consider supporting me with a small donation.

So I love how many of us love the original benchy. The only thing I've always found a little pity it can't swim.

Since I have drawn a few ships so far, I just wanted to try to draw a small, floating benchmark boat. Of course, it's not seaworthy. I also wanted to stay very close to the printing time of the original.

V2 IS HERE: https://www.printables.com/model/1152427-openvessel-20-a-practical-3d-printing-benchmark


Introducing OpenVessel, a model designed from scratch to embody the true spirit of 3D printing: freedom, openness, and community. OpenVessel provides all the benchmarking utility you need, without the unnecessary baggage or restrictions.

Features:

Original Design: Created entirely from scratch. Shapr3D source file included for transparency and adaptability.

File Formats: STL, 3MF, and STEP files available, ensuring compatibility and ease of use.

Fully Editable: Modify and adapt the design however you see fit. It’s yours to improve and share.


Enjoy!

Made from a normal Benchy, Clay Rade's tentacles, and inspired by BUT NOT REMIXED FROM BECAUSE ITS NOT PERMITTED https://www.printables.com/model/350583-benchy-organic-support-test . Also I used a random water splash model I found elsewhere for the base because I am not good at being creative. 

Gcode included in case you can't figure out how to use organic supports. It's old though, probably using prusaslicer 2.6.0 alpha 2 or 3 or something. Don't trust it I have no idea what I'm doing.

I printed mine using organic supports, generated by one of the Prusaslicer 2.6.0 alpha versions. 0.40mm nozzle 0.15m layer height as per the attached gcode.

 

UPDATE 2023 May 11: As per request, added kraken benchy with no benchy.stl which is just the tentacle part and base with a negative benchy volume instead of a benchy. See the pics (grey and red) for my test print/demo. You can print your own benchy and slip it in there! It might be a little tight to get in, but it's doable. As long as its… mostly to the official spec. Test print for that was .40mm nozzle .20mm layer height in PETG, sliced in Prusa 2.6.0 alpha-6 with automatic support painting then organic supports - they pulled right off with no issue.

💫 Recommendations

↕ Two print sizes:

  • larger base - for better grip, more weight, more leverage

 

🔄 Two printing options:

⭐ One filament

  • the whole figure + the base will be printed in one colour

🌟 More filaments (colors)

  • using the slicer/M600 or otherwise you can print the base in one color and the figure in another color
  • who has MMU/AMS/... it's even better

Booenchy, the Halloween Ghost Benchy. You can even put this costume over your Benchy and transform into a hilarious and haunting specter. With draped cloth and perfectly placed eye holes, Booenchy captures the timeless charm of a classic ghost costume, giving Benchy a spine-tingling makeover that's both funny and fun. Whether you're a Benchy enthusiast or just looking for a playful twist on 3D printing, this must-have accessory adds a boo-tiful touch to your Halloween festivities. Download the 3D model today and let the hauntingly good times begin!

Booenchy prints at spooky fast speeds, ensuring you'll have your eerie Benchy ghost costume ready to haunt in no time. What's even better? You won't need any supports to print Booenchy, making the entire process hassle-free. But here's where the real fun begins: Booenchy looks absolutely stunning when printed in Silk or multi-color PLA filaments, as these materials showcase the fabric folds in all their glory. Of course, classic white is a timeless choice that perfectly captures the essence of a ghostly apparition.

And here's the spooky cherry on top – you can take your Booenchy to the next level by placing a small LED tea light underneath it, creating an eerie and captivating glow that's bound to send shivers down spines. But the surprises don't end there! For an extra dose of whimsy, try placing a regular Benchy inside Booenchy and gently press down on the smokestack. You'll witness the magic as Benchy's eyes wink mischievously, adding a playful twist to your 3D-printed Halloween masterpiece. So, don't wait any longer – get your Booenchy 3D model today and let the printing adventures begin!

Booenchy, the enchantingly spooky 3D creation, is a result of a seamless blend of 3D sculpture and visual effects simulation. Crafted with meticulous attention to detail, Booenchy's design combines the artistry of 3D sculpting with the magic of visual effects to bring you a Halloween costume for Benchy like no other.

Happy 3D printing!
